claude.sample_unit: raters (15 physicians, 15 nurses, 15 nonhealthcare professionals) rating 15 questions x 3 response types

links.outcome: Rated medical validity and empathy of physician-revised LLM drafts versus AI-only and physician-only responses
links.effect: Physician-AI collaborative responses rated higher than AI-only and physician-only for medical validity (median 4.0 vs 3.5 and 3.7) and empathy (HCP 4.3 vs 3.2 and 3.2); all P<0.001 in primary analyses (non-HCP empathy P=0.019).
links.quote: In the primary analyses, physician–AI collaborative responses received higher ratings than both physician-only and AI-only responses across all three primary outcomes.

links.outcome: Compared physician-with-AI collaboration against physician alone and AI alone on rated quality
links.effect: Collaborative responses had higher odds of score ≥4 for medical validity (OR 3.20 vs physician-only; 5.10 vs AI-only) and empathy (OR 7.63 and 7.94 for HCP). Contribution of LLM draft could not be separated from two-stage revision.
links.quote: Thus, the higher ratings of physician–AI collaborative responses were consistent across analyses, whereas the difference between physician-only and AI-only responses depended on the analytic approach.

links.outcome: medical validity and empathy of patient explanations
links.effect: Collaborative vs AI-only: medical validity median 4.0 vs 3.5 (P<0.001); HCP empathy 4.3 vs 3.2 (P<0.001); non-HCP empathy 4.1 vs 3.3 (P=0.019).
links.quote: In the primary analyses, physician-AI collaborative responses received significantly higher ratings than both physician-only and AI-only responses across all three prespecified primary outcomes.

links.effect: AI-only high medical-validity ratings were 53.3% (36.6–69.2), versus physician-only 64.6% and physician–AI 85.4%; AI-only median 3.5 (3.0–3.7).
links.quote: In the exploratory analysis, the estimated proportions of scores ≥ 4 were 85.4%, 64.6%, and 53.3% in the physician–AI collaborative, physician-only, and AI-only groups, respectively (Table 5 ).

links.effect: AI-only high-empathy ratings were 42.1% for HCP and 35.6% for non-HCP; physician–AI collaborative responses were 85.2% and 75.9%.
links.quote: In the exploratory analysis, the estimated proportions of scores ≥ 4 were 85.2%, 43.0%, and 42.1% in the physician–AI collaborative, physician-only, and AI-only groups, respectively (Table 5 ).

links.effect: Primary comparisons: medical validity P=0.210; HCP empathy and non-HCP empathy P>0.999. Sensitivity: AI-only lower medical validity −0.17, higher non-HCP empathy 0.22.
links.quote: By contrast, comparisons between physician-only and AI-only responses varied across analytic approaches: no significant differences were observed for any outcome in the primary analyses, whereas a difference in medical validity was observed in both the sensitivity and exploratory analyses, and a difference in empathy rated by nonhealthcare professionals was observed only in the sensitivity analyses.

screen.practice: physician review and revision of LLM drafts
screen.reason: The study empirically tests the safeguard/deployment practice of physician review and revision of AI-generated responses (physician-in-the-loop draft editing) compared to AI-only or physician-only responses using simulated ICU end-of-life scenarios.
